question: In July 2022, during a photo opportunity in Baku following the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen hailed the local dictator, President İlham Əliyev, as a ‘reliable, trustworthy partner’ with whom she also wanted to conclude a bilateral agreement.

Given that 100 000 Christian Armenians were brutally displaced from Nagorno-Karabakh in the autumn of 2023 and in light of Azerbaijan’s renewed threats of war, can the Commission say whether the President still considers İlham Əliyev to be a ‘reliable, trustworthy partner’?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (24.6.2024) The Memorandum of Understanding on Energy signed on 18 July 20221 with Azerbaijan is part of the EU’s efforts to diversify its energy sources and decrease dependence on Russia, in the context of which Azerbaijan has effectively been a reliable partner.

Energy cooperation with Azerbaijan also reflects a shared ambition to accelerate the development and deployment of renewable energy generation. The EU calls on Azerbaijan to use the momentum of the annual United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP29) to step up efforts towards reaching the objectives of the Paris Agreement2.

Cooperation in the field of energy does not prejudice the EU’s stance in the normalisation process between Armenia and Azerbaijan, and is not done at the expense of the dialogue with Azerbaijan on human rights and democracy, which remains a priority. The EU continues to engage with Azerbaijan as part of the regular Human Rights Dialogue as well as in bilateral contacts.
The EU continues to call upon Azerbaijan to ensure the rights of Karabakh Armenians, including their right to return to their homes without intimidation and discrimination3.

The EU remains fully committed to facilitating dialogue between Armenia and Azerbaijan, notably under the President of the European Council’s auspices with the EU Special Representative’s support, in order to ensure long-lasting peace for the benefit of all people of the region.
